question:
In my current dbt project, each time a dbt model is run, a new container is created, and run the command dbt run --select <model name>. So, each time it runs, the whole dbt project needs to compile, which executes a lot of queries in order to compile the models. This leads to more workload on the query engine, and takes a lot of time to compile.

I have already tried the partial parsing, but that's not what I am looking for. It just reduces parsing time, but the models still need to be compiled.

Is there a way to run dbt run with already compiled models in targets/, without re-compiling? Or any better strategy to deal with this problem if dbt run without compilation is not possible.

Thanks!
title: dbt run with compiled models without re-compilation
answer:
Basically no, you cannot run dbt models without first compiling them. This is by design, as explained here: https://discourse.getdbt.com/t/run-dbt-without-compiling/2114 (a little dated but still applies).

Compiling the models is an inherent part of the run (or build) operation as this is an essential part of constructing the DAG so that dbt understands the relationships and therefore order of operations, so dbt does not provide a way to bypass that.

The new "dbt Fusion" engine apparently significantly reduces overall parse and compile time, but whether it reduces the number of metadata queries I don't know.
